_comment: T157 — the fixture that withdraws an admitted target's published specification and later restores it (SC-021). Read `README.md` before reading a result off this directory: SC-021 is a CONFORMANCE test against a fixture derived from FR-047, and FR-047 ships with zero supporting evidence because E13 never ran. This corpus does not change that and must not be written up as though it does.

configured._comment: A configured default marked unvalidated under FR-043. T149 requires it measured as WALL CLOCK FROM THE LAST SUCCESSFUL FETCH, which is what `age_seconds` is recomputed as here — not from the moment staleness was entered, because lengthening the re-fetch interval would then silently widen the ceiling.

_comment_boundary: No call in this corpus falls exactly on the ceiling. The disposition of an age of EXACTLY 900 s is T149's and T150's to state, and inventing one here would pre-empt a decision with a fixture. Every call is strictly below or strictly above.

baseline_anchor._comment: Every last-known-good set is asserted to be a subset of the reference application's published operation set.

scenarios.why: NEGATIVE CONTROL for SC-021's fourth clause. The specification goes absent and comes back IDENTICAL. Zero operations differ, so zero drift may be reported. A detector that treats every restoration as a change scores 100% on `100% of the operations that differ are reported as drift` for the scenarios where something did differ, and this is the scenario where it is caught.

The specification is unreadable by the credential — a different FR-044 non-admissible state from `absent`, and one where a document exists and nobody read it — and comes back CHANGED. Two operations are gone and one is new, so three differ and all three must be reported as drift rather than adopted silently. FR-047's own words are that a re-fetch which merely succeeds is not evidence that nothing changed.

The specification never comes back. Two calls below the ceiling are served with a stale marking; two above it are denied. This is the only scenario carrying SC-021's second and third clauses. T150 names the in-flight terminal state `terminated.staleness_ceiling_reached` — see `expected_terminal_state` below.

in_flight_session_at_ceiling._comment: T150 landed `terminated.staleness_ceiling_reached`. The previous null, and `test_the_taxonomy_still_has_no_terminal_state_naming_the_staleness_ceiling`, were the tripwire that this pass was supposed to trip. The replacement asserts this name and fails if it later vanishes.

scenarios.why: NEGATIVE CONTROL for the corpus as a whole. The specification is published at every one of four fetches. Zero results carry a stale marking, zero calls are denied, and no session terminates. SC-021's first clause reads `100% of results returned WHILE THE SET IS STALE`, whose denominator is zero here — and an implementation that marks every result stale satisfies that clause vacuously on a corpus in which the set is always stale. This is the scenario where it fails instead.

The third of FR-044's three non-admissible states — the specification is fetched successfully and describes no operations. T147 enters the stale state on the first re-fetch returning ANY of the three, and a corpus exercising only `absent` would leave two thirds of that rule unexercised. A document that parses and is empty is the state most likely to be mistaken for a successful fetch.
